The Trench Funnel primitive synthesizes injury status and in-season NGS data into a dynamic leverage model. Each injury listed (e.g., James Thompson Jr., Marques Sigle) triggers a unit rotation shift, which modifies snap share and pressure distribution. This is modeled as L_leverage = f(R_rotation, S_snap), where R_rotation quantifies depth loss and S_snap reflects positional dominance. Simultaneously, NGS-derived metrics like RYOE and stacked box percentage provide real-time efficiency adjustments. These are aggregated into a confluence score C_confluence = Σ D_domain, capturing cross-domain consistency. The system's failure mode occurs when injury reports are pre-priced by the market, negating the funnel's value. Thus, the dual logic of the funnel is: (1) injury-induced inefficiency, (2) market mispricing. The counter-thesis posits attrition is priced, but falsification hinges on line movement post-report. The GSE interprets these as state transitions in tactical leverage, while GSI uses them for Bayesian updating of player efficiency.
